newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares dip despite strong trade in mills.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares dip despite strong trade in mills.

text.p: Egyptian share prices dipped slightly on Thursday despite active trade in popular milling stocks, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority's (CMA) overall index closed at 236.17, which is 0.18 points lower than Wednesday but still the highest level for the Cairo bourse in almost 20 months.
Volume continued to rise to an average 27.26 million pounds ($8.02 million) from 21.35 million.

"Trading was delayed slightly today by a computer problem that duplicated some transactions, but the main work was due to milling shares," said broker Walid el-Khouli from El-Rashad Securities Brokerage.
"The mills will be distributing dividends in December so people are buying them up," he added.
Upper Egypt Flour Mills was top of the milling list, rising 1.45 pounds to close at 50.00 after trade worth more than 1.80 million pounds.
East Delta Flour Mills was a close second, closing 1.25 pound higher at 40.00 after trade worth more 1.20 million pounds.
Khouli said there was strong demand for fertiliser firm Egyptian Financial and Industrial, another stock expected to distributed dividends in December. The company closed unchanged at 61.00 pounds.
The CMA index for openly traded firms fell to 345.22 points from Wednesday's 346.11 and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 168.79 from 168.74 points.
